statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail risk is low at 5 because CME equity index futures are halted for the weekend and no tradable Nasdaq-100 price path exists inside this horizon; Stress stays moderate at 40 as a carried rates and energy condition rather than an equity-structure one.
recommendation: The last observed session is consistent with functioning mean reversion: NDX retraced both of its extremes, closed below its own open and left VIX near session lows, and the August expiry cleared without one-way extension. From 21:00Z the venue is shut until the Sunday reopen, which lies beyond this horizon, so the published Tail describes the absence of a price path rather than an improvement in the rates and energy backdrop. No danger window is carried, because none can be evidenced in a closed market.
headline: Weekend halt: CME equity index futures stopped at 21:00Z after a last NQ print near 29,374.25, leaving cash NDX at 29,308.86, +0.33%, as the final observed Nasdaq-100 reference.
body:
CME equity index futures stopped trading for the week at 21:00Z and the venue is confirmed closed. NQ September's last print was near 29,374.25, about +0.25%, inside a 29,220.00-29,539.00 daily range and well below the session high. Cash NDX had already settled at 29,308.86, up 95.69 points or 0.33% from a 29,213.17 previous close, after opening at 29,359.60, trading down to 29,142.44, reclaiming the entire decline to 29,405.12 and then handing back roughly ninety-six points to finish below its own open. Both extremes were retraced, neither produced repeated extension after a failed pullback, and the August expiry cleared without one-way structure. VIX closed at 14.89, down 6.00%, near the bottom of a 14.77-15.95 range.

Tail is published at 5. The reasoning is mechanical rather than optimistic: from this slot to the end of the horizon there is no tradable Nasdaq-100 price path, so the persistent no-retracement structure that Tail measures cannot form. The retained floor is a modelling convention for a halted venue, not a judgement that the underlying regime has turned benign. Mapped policy state is EA_ON and no danger window is carried, because a narrow evidence-based window cannot be justified where no evidence can be generated.

Stress is 40 and remains a rates and energy carry. The 10-year finished at 4.74%, up about three basis points; the 30-year at 5.28% is the highest since 2007; the 2-year at 4.24% firmed roughly four basis points. The Treasury's expanded long-dated buyback, announced Wednesday and widened Thursday, has not held the long end down, and the H.15 series through 20 August confirms the direction of the week. Energy carries the remainder: WTI near $86.64 and Brent near $93.83 closed a second consecutive week of roughly five percent gains with the Strait of Hormuz still shut. Neither channel transmitted into equity price structure on Friday, but both are why a large recoverable drawdown stays plausible when trading resumes.

Internals closed split rather than aligned, which is why the mode is published as normal. Delayed latest-session context shows five of eight megacaps higher with dispersion near 1.8 percentage points, led by Tesla and Alphabet against lower Nvidia and Apple, while the semiconductor complex averaged about -0.7% with ARM and Intel the largest drags. The weekly ledger is the wider frame: Nasdaq Composite -2.0%, S&P 500 -1.4% and Dow -0.8%, a bond-driven week that Friday's advance on the strongest US flash business-activity reading in more than four years only partly repaired.

Confidence is 86. The closing index and futures levels, the day ranges, the halt itself, VIX, the Treasury curve, both crude benchmarks and the forward calendar were verified directly at this cutoff, and delayed cross-asset context was used only as confirmation. Across the remaining twenty-three slots Confidence decays with distance from the last observed print rather than because any evidence has been contradicted: the next genuinely new price-path evidence arrives at the Sunday 22:00Z futures reopen, which falls outside this horizon.

lookbackSummary: Claude coverage over the past 24 hours is partial: fourteen hourly assessments are available (01:00Z, 06:00Z, 07:00Z, 08:00Z and 11:00Z through 20:00Z) while ten clock-hours, covering the 20 August US evening and scattered overnight gaps, have no published assessment and are marked unavailable. Across the available hours Tail held a narrow 10-16 band and the mapped policy state stayed EA_ON throughout. The path is coherent: 12 overnight, a drift to 16 into the 14:00Z US cash open where the mode was published as event/whipsaw, a decay back to 13 through the afternoon, a brief 16 at 19:00Z for the concentrated August expiry close, and 10 once that close cleared without one-way extension. Stress fell steadily from 59 to 48 across the same span while Confidence rose from 83 to 88 as verified evidence accumulated.
outlookSummary: The current hour carries Tail at 5, below every published reading of the session, because CME equity index futures are confirmed halted for the week and no Nasdaq-100 price path can develop inside this slot. All twenty-three remaining slots describe the same closed market: the horizon ends at 20:00Z on Saturday, several hours before the Sunday 22:00Z futures reopen, so no live evidence can arrive before this forecast expires. Tail therefore holds a flat halted-market floor of 4 and the mapped policy state stays EA_ON in every slot. Stress eases to a 34 trough in the deep weekend hours and then drifts back toward 37 as the stock of unpriced weekend information grows and the distance to the reopen shortens; the rates and energy carry behind it, a post-2007 high in the 30-year and a second consecutive five percent weekly gain in crude with the Strait of Hormuz shut, is unchanged. Confidence decays from 86 to 71 purely as a function of age. The forward checkpoints that matter all sit beyond this window: Monday's Treasury statement on Iran, the Tuesday-to-Thursday 2-, 5- and 7-year auctions, Wednesday's combined GDP second estimate, July PCE set and Nvidia results, and the Jackson Hole symposium with a Fed Chair speech on Friday at 14:00Z.

With no tradable path in this slot, Tail sits at a halted-market floor.

forecast.analysis: Late Friday with the weekly ledger already fixed: Nasdaq Composite -2.0%, S&P 500 -1.4% and Dow -0.8%, a bond-driven week that Friday's session only partly repaired. Nothing in this slot can revise that record, so Tail holds the halted-market floor and Stress reflects the carried rates backdrop.
drivers: Weekly ledger fixed at Nasdaq Composite -2.0%, S&P 500 -1.4%, Dow -0.8%
Friday's +0.33% NDX session repaired only part of the week's bond-driven decline
No mechanism exists in a halted market to extend or reverse the weekly outcome

forecast.analysis: The calendar rolls into Saturday in Europe with every equity venue closed. Confidence begins its decay from here, not because any evidence has been contradicted, but because distance from the last observed print grows while no new price-path evidence can replace it.

forecast.analysis: The Asian handover that normally sets the overnight tone is absent this weekend. In a normal week this hour would begin generating the first structure of the next session; here it produces nothing, so the last verified state is simply carried forward unchanged.
drivers: Asian futures handover absent; no overnight tone can form
Slot would normally supply first structure of a new session
Last verified state carried forward without revision

forecast.analysis: Deep weekend hours with Tokyo and Sydney closed. Stress eases a further point because a large basket drawdown requires a tradable market to occur in, and none exists inside this slot. Tail stays at the floor rather than zero, since a residual modelling floor is retained for a halted venue.
drivers: Tokyo and Sydney closed; no regional equity reference
A basket drawdown requires a tradable venue, which this slot does not have
Floor rather than zero retained as a modelling convention for halted hours

forecast.analysis: Nothing scheduled and nothing tradable. The assessment for this hour is a statement about market availability rather than about Nasdaq-100 behaviour, and it should be read that way: the published Tail describes the absence of a price path, not an improvement in the rates or energy backdrop that drove the week.
drivers: No scheduled macro release or auction inside this slot
Published Tail describes venue availability, not an improved backdrop
Rates and energy conditions carried unchanged from the Friday close

forecast.analysis: Crypto remains the only continuously traded major reference across this window, and bitcoin's strong run into the weekend is context rather than a Nasdaq-100 price path. Any read-across would be indirect and would still require the Sunday reopen, outside this horizon, to express itself in NQ.
drivers: Crypto is the only continuously quoted major asset in this window
Bitcoin strength into the weekend is context, not an NQ price path

forecast.analysis: Gold's strong Friday close and the softer dollar are the cross-asset tells carried into the weekend. Both are consistent with the inflation and fiscal concerns that drove the long end this week, and neither can be repriced until venues reopen, so they inform Stress carry rather than this hour's Tail.
drivers: Gold closed sharply higher on delayed latest-session context
Dollar extended its decline into the Friday close
Both feed Stress carry; neither can move Tail while venues are shut

forecast.analysis: Early Saturday morning in Europe. The energy channel is the most durable of the carried risks: WTI near $86.64 and Brent near $93.83 closed a second consecutive week of roughly five percent gains, with the Strait of Hormuz still shut. That is a Stress input for next week, not a path risk for this slot.
drivers: WTI near $86.64 and Brent near $93.83 after a second ~5% weekly gain
Strait of Hormuz remains closed, keeping an energy premium in place
Energy premium is a next-week Stress input, not an in-slot path risk

forecast.analysis: Weekend geopolitical headline risk is the one variable that can genuinely change between now and the reopen. Reported Iranian conditions for reopening Hormuz and a signalled US Treasury statement on Iran early next week are known checkpoints; neither has a fixed publication time inside this slot.
drivers: Iranian conditions for reopening Hormuz reported ahead of the weekend
US Treasury signalled it will address Iran measures early next week
Neither checkpoint carries a fixed time inside this hour

forecast.analysis: European cash markets would normally be pre-positioning around this hour on a weekday; on Saturday there is no such reference. The absence removes the usual European-to-US transition risk that occasionally produces the persistent one-way structure this assessment is designed to detect.
drivers: No European cash or futures reference available on Saturday
European-to-US transition risk cannot arise inside this horizon
One-way structure detection has no input data for this slot

forecast.analysis: No macro release is scheduled anywhere in the Saturday session, so the evidence set for this hour is identical to the one verified at the Friday close. Confidence continues its slow decay purely as a function of age, while Tail and Stress hold their carried floors.
drivers: No Saturday macro releases anywhere on the verified calendar
Evidence set identical to the verified Friday close
Confidence decay driven by age alone, not by new information

forecast.analysis: The next scheduled US data point of any kind is the Chicago Fed National Activity Index on Monday at 12:30Z, well beyond this horizon. That gap is why the forecast path is deliberately flat here: there is no catalyst inside the window capable of moving the assessment.
drivers: Next scheduled US release is Monday 12:30Z, outside this horizon
Flat forecast path reflects a genuine absence of in-window catalysts
Assessment can only be revised once live evidence resumes

forecast.analysis: Looking past the horizon, next week's risk is concentrated rather than spread: Wednesday carries the Q2 GDP second estimate and the July PCE set at 12:30Z, with Nvidia's results after the US cash close the same day. Those are calendar checkpoints, not conditions observed in this slot.

Nvidia reports after the Wednesday US cash close

forecast.analysis: Stress ticks up a point as the window begins shortening toward the Sunday reopen. Nvidia's Wednesday report is the largest single-name checkpoint on the horizon for a cap-weighted index; if positioning ahead of it builds, that would be a next-week Stress and Confidence question rather than a Tail one.

Pre-event positioning would inform Stress and Confidence, not Tail
Stress carry begins rising as distance to the reopen shortens

forecast.analysis: The Jackson Hole symposium runs 27-29 August with a Fed Chair speech scheduled for Friday at 14:00Z, the first at that venue for the current Chair. It is a known multi-stage communication risk for the following week and is carried in the event calendar rather than in this hour's scores.
drivers: Jackson Hole symposium scheduled 27-29 August
Fed Chair speech scheduled Friday 28 August at 14:00Z

forecast.analysis: The Treasury auction cycle resumes Tuesday through Thursday with 2-year, 5-year and 7-year sales. Given that the long end set a post-2007 high this week, auction reception is a plausible transmission channel into equities next week; inside this slot it remains an unpriced future checkpoint.

Long end printed a post-2007 high this week, raising auction sensitivity

forecast.analysis: The week's dominant narrative was fiscal and inflation-driven repricing at the long end, with the Treasury's expanded buyback failing to hold yields down. That narrative is carried into the weekend intact, which is why Stress remains moderate rather than low even in a halted market.
drivers: Expanded Treasury buyback did not hold long-end yields down
Fiscal and inflation repricing carried into the weekend intact
Stress held moderate rather than low despite the halt

forecast.analysis: Mean reversion is untestable while the venue is shut: there are no pullbacks to be shallow, no retracements to fail and no extremes to hold. The published low Tail for this hour is a statement about that absence and should not be read as evidence that the underlying regime has become benign.

forecast.analysis: Stress drifts up another point as the horizon's remaining distance to the reopen shortens and the stock of unpriced weekend information grows. Tail stays flat because the mechanism it measures, a persistent path denying retracement, still cannot operate in a closed market.
drivers: Unpriced weekend information accumulates as the reopen approaches
Stress drift reflects accumulation, not any new observed structure

forecast.analysis: Second-to-last slot of the horizon. Confidence has decayed to the low seventies purely through age; every underlying observation still stands as verified at the Friday close, and no contradicting evidence has appeared because none can be generated while venues are closed.
drivers: Confidence in the low seventies from age alone, not contradiction
All Friday-close observations still stand as verified
No new evidence can be generated before the reopen

forecast.analysis: The horizon ends on Saturday evening, still several hours before the Sunday reopen. The next assessment cycles that can see live price action will fall after that reopen, so this final slot closes the window with carried floors rather than any forward assertion about reopening structure.
drivers: Horizon closes hours before the Sunday futures reopen
Final slot carries floors rather than asserting reopen structure
Live price-path scoring resumes only after venues reopen
